source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p39
s: During the Indus Valley Civilization, the beads manufacturing industry was located at
x: Chanhudaro was primarily a craft production site specialising in bead making. Excavations revealed bead-making furnaces, drills and workshops.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p39
s:
Select the correct statements about religious beliefs of the Rig Vedic Period :
I. Dyus was a celestial God of the Rig Vedic Aryans similar to Jupiter of the Greeks.
II. Prithvi was considered as the mother of all Gods.
III. Agni was worshipped as the intermediary of taking the offerings to the deities.
IV. Cow sacrifice was also the part of worship.
x: Dyus resembled the Greek Jupiter, Agni carried offerings to the gods, and animal sacrifice including cow sacrifice existed in the early Vedic period. Prithvi was not considered the mother of all gods, so statement II is incorrect.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p39
s: Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela gave the details of irrigation facilities provided in the Kalinga Region by
x: The Hathigumpha inscription records that an irrigation canal had been constructed earlier during the rule of Mahapadmananda of the Nanda dynasty. Kharavela later restored and improved it.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p39
s:
Select the correct statements regarding the inscriptions of Ashoka :
I. They are in Brahmi, Kharosthi, Greek and Aramaic scripts.
II. The Monarch's name was mentioned as Ashoka only in Maski and Gurjara inscriptions.
III. The XIII Rock edict mentioned the names of the five Greek Rulers as his contemporaries.
IV. The IV and V edicts mentioned the war of succession with his brothers.
x: Ashokan inscriptions were issued in Brahmi, Kharosthi, Greek and Aramaic, and the name Ashoka appears explicitly only in the Maski and Gurjara inscriptions. The XIII Rock Edict mentions contemporary Greek rulers such as Antiochus.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p39
s: Which of the following was NOT the feature of the Guilds during the Gupta Period ?
x: Guilds in the Gupta period were powerful autonomous bodies of merchants, artisans and traders with their own regulations, judicial authority and even private forces. Hence describing them as non-autonomous is incorrect.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p39
s:
The account of Greek (Yavana) invasion during the reign of Pushyamitra Sunga is available in :
I. Gargi - Samhita
II. Patanjali - Mahabhashya
III. Kalidasa - Malavikagnimitra
IV. Visakhadatta - Mudrarakshasa
x: Gargi Samhita, Patanjali's Mahabhashya and Kalidasa's Malavikagnimitra refer to Yavana invasions in the Sunga period. Visakhadatta's Mudrarakshasa deals with Mauryan history.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p40

o: Xuanzang was the Chancellor of the university.
Silabhadra was the Chancellor of the university.
Dharmapala was the Chancellor of the university.
Nagarjuna was the Chancellor of the university.
x: During Harshavardhana's reign, when Xuanzang studied at Nalanda, the university's chief scholar or chancellor was Silabhadra.

I. Ravan ki Khai
II. Kailasanatha
III. Dashavatara

s:
Which of the following highways existed during the rule of Kakatiyas ?
I. Orugallu - Tripuranthakam - Nellore
II. Dwarasamudra - Ballari - Orugallu
III. Motupalli - Tripuranthakam - Ballari
IV. Palnadu - Nalgonda - Nekarikallu - Orugallu
x: The Kakatiya kingdom maintained trade and military routes such as Motupalli-Tripuranthakam-Ballari and Palnadu-Nalgonda-Nekarikallu-Orugallu.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p40
s:
Which of the principles are common for Bhakti and Sufi movement ?
I. Monotheism
II. Asceticism
III. Religious tolerance
IV. Accepted the idol worship to some extent
x: Both movements emphasised devotion to one God, rejected rigid ritualism and encouraged religious tolerance. Idol worship was generally not accepted in Sufism.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p40
s: Choose the INCORRECT pair regarding the foreign chronicles of the Vijayanagara Period :

Nikitin - Visited during the reign of Achyuta Devaraya
Domingo Paes - Visited during the reign of Krishnadeva Raya
Barbosa - Visited during the reign of Krishnadeva Raya
x: Russian traveller Nikitin visited during the reign of Deva Raya II, not Achyuta Devaraya, so that pair is incorrect.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p40
s: The Vijayanagara ruler who permitted Jesuits to build churches at Nellore and Chandragiri was
x: Venkatapati Raya II permitted Jesuit missionaries to build churches at Nellore and Chandragiri.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p40
s:
Which of the following incidents took place during the reign of Jahangir ?
I. The fifth Sikh Guru, Arjan Dev was sentenced to death.
II. Victory over Rajputs of Mewar.
III. Annexation of Kabul and Kandahar.
IV. Arrival of English East India Company to India.
x: During Jahangir's reign (1605-1627) Guru Arjan Dev was executed (1606), peace was concluded with the Rajputs of Mewar, and the English East India Company established trade relations.

x: Sher Shah Suri's most famous road was the Grand Trunk Road, which extended from the Indus River to Sonargaon in Bengal.

s: The idea of Indian Constituent Assembly was put forward for the first time by
x: The idea of a Constituent Assembly for India was first proposed by M.N. Roy in 1934. It was later adopted by the Congress and implemented in 1946.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p42
s:
Which of the following institutions were NOT established during the Non-Cooperation Movement ?
I. Besant Theosophical College, Madanapalle
II. Jamia Millia Islamia, Delhi
III. Kashi Vidyapith, Benaras
IV. Aligarh Muslim University, Aligarh
x: Jamia Millia Islamia and Kashi Vidyapith were national institutions founded during the Non-Cooperation Movement. Besant Theosophical College and Aligarh Muslim University were established earlier.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p42
s: The Indian Independence Bill was introduced in the House of Commons by the British Prime Minister Attlee on
x: The Indian Independence Bill was introduced by Clement Attlee on 4 July 1947 and received royal assent on 18 July 1947.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p42
s:
Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the State Finance Commission ?
I. It is required to appoint a State Finance Commission once in five years.
II. It recommends the determination of taxes, duties, tolls and fees assigned to the Panchayats and Municipalities.
III. Article 243 deals with constitution of finance commission to review financial position of Panchayats.
x: Article 243-I provides for a State Finance Commission constituted by the Governor every five years to review Panchayat finances. It recommends distribution of taxes, duties, tolls and fees between the state and local bodies.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p42
s:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the correct code :
Assertion (A) : The President is the executive power of the Union.
Reason (R) : The executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President and shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with the Constitution.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
x: Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President, exercised directly or through subordinate officers. In practice it is exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p42
s:
Which of the following statements related to the Central Administrative Tribunal are correct ?
I. It is a statutory body.
II. Its members are drawn from administrative background only.
III. It is not bound by the procedure prescribed in the Code of Civil Procedure.
IV. Its jurisdiction covers the members of All-India services as well as Central services and Central Government posts.
V. It was set up in 1985.
x: The CAT was established under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, and covers All-India Services and central government employees. Its members include both judicial and administrative experts.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p42
s: Which of the following statement(s) is/are NOT one of the powers of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly ?
o: He has original vote in all matters.
He has no veto except in case of a tie.
The Speaker will NOT preside when a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration of the Assembly.
x: The Speaker does not possess veto powers except a casting vote in case of a tie. When a resolution for his removal is under consideration, he does not preside over the House.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p42
s:
The powers of the Election Commission include which of the following ?
I. The Election Commission takes decisions on every aspect of conduct and control of elections from the announcement of elections to the declaration of results.
II. During the election period, the Election Commission can order the Government to dismiss some government officials.
III. When on election duty, Government officers work under the control of the Election Commission.
x: The ECI supervises and controls elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President. During elections, officers on election duty function under its control.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p43
s:
What is/are the provision(s) to safeguard the autonomy of the Supreme Court of India ?
I. While appointing the Supreme Court Judges, the President of India has to consult the Chief Justice of India.
II. The Supreme Court Judges can be removed by the Chief Justice of India only.
III. The salaries of the Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India on which the legislature does not have to vote.
x: Supreme Court judges are appointed by the President in consultation with the CJI, and their salaries are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, which Parliament does not vote on.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p43
s:
Which of the following are NOT included in the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court ?
I. A dispute between two or more States.
II. A dispute regarding elections to either House of the Parliament or that of Legislature of a State.
III. A dispute between the Government of India and a Union Territory.
IV. A dispute between the Government of India and one or more States.
x: Original jurisdiction under Article 131 covers disputes between the Union and States or between States. Election disputes and disputes involving Union Territories do not fall under it.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p43
s:
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes, while investigating any matter or inquiring into any complaint, has the powers on the following matters :
I. It can receive evidences on affidavits.
II. It can requisition any public record from any court or office.
III. It can issue summons for the examination of witnesses and documents.
x: While investigating complaints, the NCSC has powers of a civil court, including summoning witnesses, receiving evidence on affidavits and requisitioning public records.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p43
s:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the correct code :
Assertion (A) : The Parliament of India consists of the President and two Houses.
Reason (R) : The President is a part of the legislature even though he does not sit in Parliament except for the purpose of delivering his opening address.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
x: Article 79 states that Parliament consists of the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. The President is an integral part of the legislature because no bill becomes law without his assent.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p43
s:
Which of the following are among the Fundamental Duties of citizens laid down in the Indian Constitution ?
I. To protect the weaker sections from social injustice.
II. To develop scientific temper and spirit of inquiry.
III. To preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
IV. To safeguard public property and adjure violence.
x: The Fundamental Duties added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) include developing scientific temper, preserving India's composite culture and safeguarding public property while abjuring violence.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p43
s: Which of the following entries of the Indian Constitution deals with the institutions for scientific or technical education financed by the Government of India, wholly or in part, and declared by Parliament, by law to be institutions of national importance ?
x: Entry 64 of the Union List deals with institutions for scientific or technical education declared by Parliament as institutions of national importance, such as IITs and AIIMS.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p43
s: Who said "India is not a nation in the traditional western sense but a comprehensive culture of continental scope compounded of a very large number of linguistic and religious entities, highly complex and often strongly antagonistic local cultures" ?
x: Political scientist Carl J. Friedrich described India as a civilizational entity with diverse linguistic and cultural groups rather than a homogeneous nation-state.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p43
s:
The Constitution confers which of the following Articles that denies the rights to aliens (Foreign Citizens) ?
I. Articles 29 and 30
II. Article 19
III. Articles 23 and 24
IV. Article 16
x: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29 and 30 provide rights specifically to citizens, whereas rights like Articles 14 and 21 apply to everyone.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p44
s:
Consider the following statements :
I. The Preamble was enacted before the enactment of the entire Constitution.
II. The Preamble is a part of the Constitution but has no legal effect independently of other parts.
III. It is enforceable through Courts of Law.
IV. The Objectives Resolution by Jawaharlal Nehru finally became the foundation for the Preamble.
Which of the statements given above are INCORRECT?
x: The Preamble was adopted along with the Constitution in 1949, not before it, so statement I is incorrect. Although part of the Constitution, it is not directly enforceable in courts.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p44
s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct
I. The PM CARES for Children Scheme was launched by the Prime Minister of India on 29th May, 2021 for the children.
II. It aims to support children who have lost both the parents or legal guardians or adoptive parents or surviving parent to Covid-19 pandemic.
x: The PM CARES for Children Scheme was launched in May 2021 to support children who lost parents or guardians to the COVID-19 pandemic.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p44
s: With child labour being made illegal and right to education becoming a fundamental right for children, this right against exploitation has become more meaningful. Which of the following pairs of Articles provide for right to education and prohibition of child labour respectively ?
x: Article 21A guarantees free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14 years. Article 24 prohibits employment of children below 14 years in hazardous industries.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p44
s:
Consider the following statements regarding GST
I. GST will bring more transparency to direct tax laws.
II. GST was the 122nd Constitutional Amendment Bill introduced in the Parliament.
III. GST is a destination-based tax.
x: GST was introduced through the 122nd Constitutional Amendment Bill, enacted as the 101st Amendment Act (2016). It is a destination-based tax.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p44
s: Which of the bodies recommends the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes to be shared between the Centre and the States, and allocation between the States, the respective shares of such proceeds
x: The Finance Commission, constituted under Article 280, recommends the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and the States and among the States.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p44
s: Which of the following is NOT the function of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes ?
o: To investigate and monitor all matters relating to the safeguards provided for the Scheduled Castes under the Constitution.
To submit the report to the Prime Minister related to the protection of Scheduled Castes.
To inquire into specific complaints with respect to the deprivation of rights and safeguards of the Scheduled Castes.
To advise on the planning process of socio-economic development of the Scheduled Castes.
x: The NCSC submits its reports to the President of India, not to the Prime Minister. The President places them before Parliament.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p44
s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) ?
o: Conducting examinations for appointments to the services of the Union.
Advising on matters relating to methods of recruitment.
x: The UPSC conducts recruitment examinations and advises on recruitment methods. The policy of reservation is decided by the government, not by UPSC.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p44
s:
Which of the following subjects are listed in the 11th Schedule ?
I. Women and Child Development
II. Public Distribution System
III. Libraries
IV. Slum Improvement and Upgradation
V. Markets and Fairs
x: The 11th Schedule, added by the 73rd Amendment, lists 29 subjects for Panchayats including women and child development, public distribution system, libraries, and markets and fairs. Slum improvement belongs to the 12th Schedule.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p44
s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the National Green Tribunal ?
I. It was set up under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
II. NGT is bound by the procedure laid down under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
III. NGT has six places of sitting throughout the country.
x: The NGT was established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010. Unlike regular courts, it is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p45
s:
With reference to the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019, consider the following statements about National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) :
I. Judge of the Supreme Court can now be appointed as Chairperson of the Commission.
II. Term of the Chairperson and members shall be three years.
III. Chairperson and members shall be eligible for re-appointment.
x: The 2019 amendment allowed a Supreme Court judge to serve as NHRC chairperson, reduced the tenure to three years and permitted reappointment of members.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p45
s:
With reference to the National Commission for Minorities, consider the following statements :
I. It was set up under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
II. Ministry of Welfare has notified five religious communities under "Minority" status, to date.
III. It can make recommendations for the effective implementation of safeguards for the protection of minorities by Central or State Governments.
x: The National Commission for Minorities was established under the NCM Act, 1992. It monitors safeguards for minorities and recommends measures for their protection.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p45
s: Recently, the term "Chicago Convention" is frequently seen in the news. Which of the following sector is it associated with ?
x: The Chicago Convention (1944) established the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) and laid down rules governing international civil aviation.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p45
s:
With reference to the Competition Commission of India, consider the following statements :
I. It is a statutory body established under Competition Act, 2002 as amended by the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2007.
II. It consists of a chairperson and five members appointed by the Central Government.
x: The CCI is a statutory body under the Competition Act, 2002. It originally consisted of a chairperson and up to six members, not five.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p45
s: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was established on the recommendation of which of the following Committee ?
x: NABARD was established in 1982 on the recommendation of the Sivaraman Committee (CRAFICARD).

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p45
s: "World Competitiveness Index" is released by which of the following organizations ?
x: The World Competitiveness Index is published by the Institute for Management Development (IMD) based in Switzerland.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p45
s: Kautilya categorizes the Governments and Heads of Departments into 18 tirthas. Amongst these "Dandapala" is the
x: In the Arthashastra, Kautilya described 18 major administrative officials called Tirthas. The Dandapala was responsible for military affairs and maintaining order within the army.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p45
s:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select your answer from the codes given below.
Assertion (A) : There is a structural change in the composition of National Income in India.
Reason (R) : The process of economic growth was initiated in India.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation for (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation for (A).
x: The share of agriculture in India's GDP has declined while industry and services have expanded, indicating structural change. This shift is linked to the process of economic growth and development.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p46
s: The economist who said that the "Net Social Product and the Social Income are one and the same thing" is
x: J.R. Hicks stated that Net Social Product and Social Income are essentially the same concept in national income accounting.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p46
s:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select your answer from the codes given below.
Assertion (A) : Per Capita Income decreases in a developing country even though National Income increases.
Reason (R) : The rate of growth of population is higher than the rate of growth of National Income.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation for (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation for (A).
x: Per capita income is national income divided by population. If population growth exceeds national income growth, per capita income can decline even as national income rises.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p46
s: During which Five Year Plan was the rate of growth of Gross Domestic Product the highest ?
x: The 11th Five Year Plan (2007-2012) recorded the highest GDP growth among the planning periods, averaging around 8%.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p46
s: What is the age-group of higher proportion of working population required for Demographic Dividend ?
x: A demographic dividend occurs when the proportion of working-age population (15-64 years) is higher compared to dependents.

s:
Which of the following are the objectives of Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao ?
I. To provide legal assistance to girls
II. To reduce decline in Child Sex Ratio
III. To encourage women empowerment
IV. To remove gender inequality
x: The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme aims to improve the child sex ratio, promote girls' education and empower women, thereby reducing gender discrimination.

Assertion (A) : National Income growth fluctuates with fluctuations in Agriculture growth in India.
Reason (R) : Weather conditions, especially rains, are uncertain in India.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation for (A).

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p46
s:
When the Central Bank increases the Cash Reserve Ratio, it leads to
I. Fall in money circulation.
II. Low demand for goods and services.
III. Rise in purchasing power of the people.
IV. Rise in bank's lending capacity
x: When CRR is increased, banks must keep more deposits with the RBI, reducing lending and money circulation. This lowers demand for goods and services, helping control inflation.

source: latestpyqs Shreshta APPSC Group-1 & 2 Prelims & Mains PYQs (b3p1) p47
s:
Statutory Liquidity Ratio is to be maintained by banks in the form of
I. Cash.
II. Gold.
III. Unencumbered investments in specified instruments
IV. Priority sector loans
x: SLR requires banks to maintain a percentage of their deposits in liquid assets such as cash, gold and approved government securities.

s: Gilt edged market comprises
o: Treasury Bills and Government Bond Market
x: The gilt-edged market is the market for government securities such as treasury bills and government bonds, considered safe because they are backed by the government.

o: A loan whose instalment of principal and interest amount has remained overdue for a period of 60 days.
A loan whose instalment of principal and interest amount has remained overdue for a period of 90 days.
A loan whose instalment of principal and interest amount has remained overdue for a period of 180 days.
A loan whose instalment of principal and interest amount has remained overdue for a period of 30 days.
x: A Non-Performing Asset is a loan on which interest or principal payments remain overdue for more than 90 days.

o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation for (A).
